area: Team server mode: accounts, roles, per-tenant-profile entitlements on every route, sign-in hardening, SCIM 2.0, built-in HTTPS (own, self-signed, ACME dns-01), four-eyes with real identities, audit scoping, sharing, encryption at rest and FIPS mode
title: Wave 7: an optional multi-user team server, deny by default, with the single-user default unchanged

checks.what: Every registered route (and mount) has a team access rule or is on the explicit public list; the public /api/ routes are only sign-in, liveness and status
A route with no rule is 403 on a team server, even for an administrator; every protected route is 401 to an anonymous caller; every admin route is 403 to the other roles

Per-tenant-profile entitlements: a viewer signs in only to granted profiles; no profile, another profile or typed details for another tenant are refused before any sign-in; roles cap grants; reports, jobs and records are bound to maker and profile
Lockout enforced even with the right password, unlocks by administrator or time; unknown names answer and lock the same; per-address sign-in limit
Session cookie HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, Secure over HTTPS; new id at sign-in; idle and absolute timeouts; role change and disable end sessions; UI token refused in every form
Cross-site and Origin-less changes carrying the session cookie are refused
SCIM: bearer token required, stored as SHA-256, shown once, revocable; a session is not the SCIM credential; SCIM cannot make an administrator; 404 outside team mode
A team server beyond loopback (local or container publish) refuses to start without HTTPS; the older ways start with a loud warning; HSTS only on a team server over HTTPS
Four-eyes on a team server: requester cannot approve (even admin, even with DLP_CHECK_FOUR_EYES=0); approver needs approve on the request's profile
Audit entries carry the actor (jobs included) and the tenant profile; viewers see only entries of profiles they may read
Every local store sealed with AES-256-GCM when enabled, survives key rotation (old key forgotten), tampering detected, self-healing reads sealed stores
ACME dns-01 through Cloudflare against fakes: valid ES256 JWS and nonces, correct TXT value, record removed, certificate matches key and names; https and same-host directory only
Single-user default unchanged: all existing auth, SSO, UI token and change-queue tests pass with team mode off

findings.title: The shared-plan check passed every caller inside the access middleware, because it read the request context before the middleware had set it
findings.fix: team_server.may_use takes the caller explicitly; the middleware passes it

findings.title: Approve and reject on the change queue called the writer check, so an approver (who may not apply) could never approve on a team server
findings.fix: On an approve route the approve right stands in for the writer check (security.may_write); change_queue.decide re-checks approve on the request's profile

findings.title: Self-healing would have moved encrypted stores aside as corrupt
findings.fix: self_heal._parse opens a sealed store before checking it

findings.title: SAML sign-in is not built in: safe SAML needs an XML-signature library (xmlsec) that is not pinned
findings.fix: Documented in SECURITY.md and INSTALL.md; use the provider's OpenID Connect app

findings.title: Passkeys (WebAuthn) are not built in: no vetted WebAuthn library is in the hash-pinned lock
findings.fix: Documented; prefer SSO with the provider's MFA

findings.title: FIPS mode restricts the app's own algorithms but the Python and OpenSSL builds are not a FIPS 140-3 validated module; TLS 1.3 suites are the platform's
findings.fix: Said plainly in store_crypto.fips_status, the Team server page and SECURITY.md
